How Does Central Identity Federation Unify Multi-Tenant SSO, Custom Domains & Dual-RP Passkeys?

Long image

A

Answer

SCRIPE decouples interactive identity workflows (https://auth.scripe.org) from protocol callback ingress (https://api.scripe.org) while keeping custom tenant domains, native admin logins, WebAuthn passkeys, Sudo step-up, and split logouts strictly fail-closed.

  1. Central Callback & Single-Use Handoff: External OIDC (GET /api/v1/auth/oidc/callback) and SAML (POST /api/v1/auth/saml/acs/{providerId}) callbacks on api.scripe.org consume server-side ExternalAuthStateTicket (never client sessionStorage), mint a 120s SHA-256 ExternalAuthHandoffTicket, and redeem it once via POST /api/v1/auth/sso/handoff.
  2. Custom-Domain First-Party HMAC Relay: Verified custom domains cannot share cross-site cookies with api.scripe.org, so Next.js BFF exposes /api/auth/session/{establish,refresh,logout} guarded by HMAC-SHA256 headers and issuing __Host-scripe_refresh_token (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax).
  3. Dynamic Origin Governance & Dual-RP Passkeys: IVerifiedOriginEvaluator feeds dynamic CORS/CSRF checks with a 60s generation-keyed cache, while AdminPasskey.RpId / WebAuthnChallenge.RpId keep EnableCentralNativeAndPasskeyMigration locked false on admin.scripe.org and *.admin.scripe.org.
  4. Sudo Expansion, Sibling-JTI Revoke & Split Logout: <SudoVerificationModal /> expands 403 retry across Sudo revocation/downgrade errors, RevokeAllSessions preserves the caller's session via sibling JTI blacklisting, and AuthLogoutScopeHelper preserves scr.oidc.session on "app" logouts.

Applies toSCRIPE-Backend + SCRIPE-Frontend + SCRIPE-CLIStage 6B

How Do Central Auth, API Callbacks, Custom-Domain Relay & Native Origins Connect?

Diagram structure
  • auth.scripe.org fe_auth
  • Custom Tenant BFF fe_custom
  • admin.scripe.org fe_native
  • api.scripe.org api_cb
  • Relay, Sudo & Dual-RP sec_gate
  • Redis + SQL Store id_store
  • fe_auth → api_cb · OIDC/SAML
  • fe_custom → sec_gate · HMAC BFF
  • sec_gate → api_cb · /sso/handoff
  • fe_native → sec_gate · WebAuthn + Sudo
  • api_cb → id_store
  • sec_gate → id_store

Click any highlighted node below to step through host boundaries, cookie isolation, HMAC relay signing, Dual-RP WebAuthn, and Sudo enforcement across both repositories.

  1. auth.scripe.org UI ↗

    Interactive SSO start, /sso/continue workspace picker & 2FA challenge (Tenancy:AuthBaseUrl, OpenIddict:FrontendBaseUrl).

  2. Custom-Domain BFF Relay ↗

    Next.js /api/auth/session/{establish,refresh,logout} checks same-origin headers, signs X-Scripe-Session-Relay-*, and sets __Host-scripe_refresh_token (Lax).

  3. Native & Passkey Origin ↗

    Locked on admin.scripe.org and *.admin.scripe.org (EnableCentralNativeAndPasskeyMigration: false) with OriginRouting + BroadcastChannel isolation.

  4. Central Callback Ingress ↗

    OidcClientController.Central and SAML ACS redeem server ExternalAuthStateTicket, mint 120s SHA-256 ExternalAuthHandoffTicket, and 302 redirect.

  5. Relay, Dual-RP & Sudo Gate ↗

    SessionRelayAuthenticator (30s skew, 60s nonce), IVerifiedOriginEvaluator, Fido2PasskeyService.ResolveAndValidateRpId, RevokeAllSessions JTI blacklist, and AuthLogoutScopeHelper.

  6. Redis + SQL Persistence ↗

    Stores auth:ext-handoff-used:{sha256}, relay nonces, AdminPasskey.RpId (varchar(253)), and hashed RefreshTokens.

How Do Central Callback, Custom-Domain Relay & Split Logout Execute Step by Step?

Custom-domain workspaces route refresh tokens through their own Next.js first-party BFF (__Host-scripe_refresh_token) while keeping scr.oidc.session isolated until explicit "central" logout.

Diagram structure
  • Custom Domain SPA spa
  • Next.js HMAC Relay bff
  • api.scripe.org api
  • Relay & Store sec
  • External IdP idp
  • spa → api · POST /api/v1/auth/oidc/challenge
  • api → spa · idpUrl (ExternalAuthStateTicket cached)
  • spa → idp · authenticate at IdP
  • idp → api · GET /api/v1/auth/oidc/callback
  • api → sec · mint 120s SHA-256 HandoffTicket
  • api → spa · 302 {ReturnOrigin}/sso/callback?code=
  • spa → bff · POST /api/auth/session/establish
  • bff → api · HMAC X-Scripe-Session-Relay-* + /sso/handoff
  • api → sec · atomic claim auth:ext-handoff-used:{sha256}
  • bff → spa · Access JWT JSON + __Host-scripe_refresh_token
  • spa → bff · POST /api/auth/session/logout (app default)
  • bff → api · revoke refresh cookie (keep scr.oidc.session)

Decision 2: Why Native Admin Login & Passkeys Stay Locked on admin.scripe.org

CentralFederationOptions.EnableCentralNativeAndPasskeyMigration stays false in all environments. Existing AdminPasskey credentials bind cryptographically to the registering Relying Party (rpId); migrating native login to auth.scripe.org without Dual-RP opt-in would orphan enrolled hardware keys. Adding AdminPasskey.RpId (varchar(253), backfilled 'admin.scripe.org') and AllowedRpIds provides non-breaking forward compatibility.
